plan.title: Adipose treated vs control DE adjusted for sex/age
plan.analytical_narrative: 12 adipose samples (6 treated, 6 control), unpaired, single batch, salmon-derived raw gene-level counts (12000 genes x 12 samples in the count matrix; the 13th column is the gene-symbol column), with sex and age recorded per sample and the groups not age-matched. Age and sex are potential confounders of a treated-vs-control comparison, so age is entered as a continuous covariate and sex as a fixed factor in the DESeq2 design (~ sex + age + condition) rather than removed by a pre-hoc adjustment, per consensus guidance that covariate correction belongs inside the count model. Track 1 runs sample-structure QC (blinded VST, PCA, sample-distance heatmap colored by condition, sex, and age) to check whether age/sex or an outlier sample dominates the variance structure before any test is trusted, then the DESeq2 Wald test with a minimal count pre-filter, size-factor normalization, apeglm shrinkage of the treated-vs-control coefficient, and BH-adjusted independent filtering at alpha 0.05, with a p-value histogram and MA/dispersion diagnostics to check the fit before genes are called significant. Track 2 takes the full ranked gene list (Wald statistic) into fgsea preranked GSEA against MSigDB Hallmark (primary) and Reactome (secondary) gene sets for human, since with 12 samples an over-representation test on a possibly short significant-gene list would be underpowered per the flagged rule. A final report step consolidates the DE table, diagnostics, enrichment results with leading-edge genes, and a full reproducibility record (session info, seed, package and gene-set collection versions).
